quote.text: You have to go and find the limit — and then a little bit further.
quote.author: — Bruce McLaren, 1963

founder.headline: A driver who built his own future.
founder.name: Bruce McLaren
paragraphs: Bruce McLaren was 22 years old when he won the United States Grand Prix in 1959 — the youngest Formula One race winner in history at the time. But winning wasn't enough. He wanted to build the car himself.

In 1963, working from a small workshop in Feltham, Middlesex, he started what would become one of the most decorated names in motorsport. His philosophy was simple and uncompromising: a lighter car is a faster car. That belief became the foundation of everything McLaren has ever built.

Bruce died in a testing accident at Goodwood in June 1970, aged 32. The team he created went on to win 8 Constructors' Championships, 12 Drivers' Championships, and produce some of the most revered road cars ever made.
founder.note: Every McLaren built today carries a small plaque bearing his name.

timeline.event: Bruce McLaren founds Bruce McLaren Motor Racing in New Zealand.
McLaren enters Formula One as a constructor for the first time.
Emerson Fittipaldi wins McLaren's first F1 Constructors' Championship.
MP4/1 becomes the first F1 car with a full carbon fibre monocoque.
Ayrton Senna and Alain Prost dominate — 15 wins from 16 races.
The McLaren F1 road car debuts — the greatest driver's car ever made.
MP4-12C launches modern McLaren road car era from Woking.
W1 hypercar unveiled — successor to the F1 with ground-effect aero.

philosophy.title: Lighter is faster.
philosophy.text: Carbon fibre is not a luxury — it is the only logical choice for a car that must be both safe and swift. Every gram removed is a gram that never has to be accelerated, braked, or cornered.

philosophy.title: The driver decides.
philosophy.text: Technology exists to extend the driver's ability, never to replace it. Our systems read inputs and respond — they do not intervene, override, or second-guess the person behind the wheel.

philosophy.title: Nothing is enough.
philosophy.text: Bruce McLaren once said you have to find the limit — and then go a little further. That pursuit has never stopped. Every new McLaren is a reaction to everything that came before it.
